authorial_core.interpreted_intent: Requester meaning: independently choose a fitting random concept to test the context-linked Clockpunk topic and use the supplied image. The exact prior-user topic quote establishes Clockpunk, while no requester-owned mechanism, public role, camera view or louver system is supplied. General knowledge interprets Clockpunk as an alternate historical world where clockwork mechanisms materially shape life. Agent choice: after one seeded draw from four coherent civic scenes, photograph a shade keeper in a Renaissance reading court as a hand-driven louver bank brings shade to waiting readers. WHO: a fictional keeper concentrates on the adjustment; the face and hair are guided only by the visible portrait, not a biography or actual identity. WHERE: a public reading court gives the small mechanical action a social consequence. HOW: a nearby environmental view lets face, hands, drive and response coexist. WHY NOW: one reader can finally move the book from harsh sun into the first arriving shade. The intended experience is quiet attraction to the keeper and pleasure in comprehensible civic ingenuity. Saved sensual=1 subtly supports this through bearing, neckline and reflected face light; fetish=0 adds no treatment, surreal=0 keeps the physical relations grounded, and creativity=1 preserves a restrained direction with local later variations. All particular louver mechanics, garments, readers, location and framing remain agent-owned open staging. Projected planning: the figure and wheel are foreground-sized; the short linkage is arranged at the open side, with its endpoints in the same depth band, while a large shade edge makes consequence readable rather than relying on small decorative gears.

authorial_core.event: An agent-authored keeper adjusts a manual canopy drive as the first shade reaches a public reading table. Only a visible Clockpunk event is requester-derived; this specific action and apparatus are replaceable staging.
visual_priorities: The keeper grips the wheel with both hands while looking toward the louver she is checking; her portrait-guided face remains prominent.
The visible wheel spindle, meshed pinion and larger wheel establish a connected drive rather than an ornamental gear surface.
A short rod links the larger wheel to the louver tie-bar in one observable plane.
The partly tilted slats cast a clear shade band across the reading table, and a reader moves a book into it.
Keeper, functional civic architecture and readers share one inhabited space, with the mechanical chain subordinate to her concentrated presence.
authorial_core.baseline_prompt_en: Photograph a Clockpunk environment with a reference-guided human subject, caught during a visible clockwork event in a sun-struck civic reading court. The central fictional woman is the keeper of its shade canopy. Use the supplied portrait as visible face and hair guidance: a soft oval face, large dark-brown eyes, a straight nose and softly defined pink lips; a dark jaw-length bob with a lightly separated fringe. Her ink-blue square-neck linen dress and warm reflected light give her a quiet, attractive presence while her attention stays on the work. She stands beside a waist-high handwheel at the open edge of a limestone loggia, her torso angled comfortably toward it. Her right hand grips the upper rim and her left hand steadies the lower rim, both elbows bent with room beside her body. Her shoulders are relaxed and her head turns slightly toward the camera side as she looks up to check the nearest louver, keeping both eyes readable. The wheel's horizontal spindle enters a small brass pinion visibly meshed with a larger toothed wheel in an open iron frame. A crank arm on that larger wheel connects to a slender vertical rod; the rod rises in clear view to a short tie-bar attached to the pivot arms of the overhead louver bank. Broad oak slats with bronze edges sit partly tilted, their common pivots and connecting bar easy to distinguish. Worn contact surfaces and fresh polished arcs on the gear teeth suggest a mechanism used every day. The present adjustment has just brought the first broad band of shade across a stone reading table. One of two waiting readers slides an open book into that cool band, while the other still shades their eyes in the adjacent sun. The keeper watches the slat rather than performing for the camera; the readers' small responses make her effort matter. Warm limestone, dark timber and restrained brass hold the palette together. Make an inhabited environmental photograph from the open side of the loggia at the keeper's chest height, in a horizontal 4:3 frame with natural 35 mm perspective. Frame her from mid-thigh upward, placing her face and handwheel prominently in the foreground and the complete short drive linkage along the right side. Include the low canopy above and the table behind within the same readable depth. Crisp noon light makes the moving shade boundary graphic; soft reflected stone light retains the reference face's form and the hands' contact. Preserve enough depth of field to read the gear mesh, linkage endpoints and readers together, with tactile photographic skin, linen, timber and metal.
